certifyingEntity.name: Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control (DFPC)
certifyingEntity.policyManualNote: CDFPC Certification Policy and Procedure Manual (verify current revision on DFPC site)
certifyingEntity.notes: Colorado operates a voluntary firefighter and emergency services certification program. There is no statewide statutory requirement that all firefighters hold DFPC certification; departments set their own hiring and qualification rules.

accreditation.notes: DFPC is accredited by both IFSAC and the Pro Board for multiple levels including Firefighter I/II, Driver/Operator series, Fire Officer I–III, and Fire & Emergency Services Instructor I–III.

programNotes: Certification is voluntary at the state level.
Candidates for many levels must be affiliated with a Colorado Emergency Services Agency.
Certificates are typically issued for a five (5) year period (confirm current rule).
Written + practical testing is administered through DFPC processes; practicals use mandatory and randomly selected JPRs.
Firefighter I includes a live-burn practical examination component.
As of 2026, DFPC is transitioning several firefighter and driver/operator levels toward NFPA 1010 (2024 edition) with an effective date of 1 July 2026 — confirm current edition in force when testing.

reciprocity.summary: IFSAC or Pro Board accredited certifications from other entities may be eligible for Colorado recognition through DFPC reciprocity / non-accredited recognition processes.
notes: Department head or applicant submits documentation through DFPC process.
Driver/Operator series reciprocity typically requires proof of a current driver’s license.
Fees and exact packet requirements change — always use the current DFPC reciprocity instructions.
